issue.body:
Migrates this repo to use `@mui/internal-docs-infra` [`useTypes`](https://deploy-preview-489--mui-internal.netlify.app/docs-infra/hooks/use-types) (added in https://github.com/mui/mui-public/pull/489). Maintains the existing design and theme.

Preview: https://deploy-preview-2932--base-ui.netlify.app/react/components/accordion#api-reference

## Improvements

- Fixes cache key issue with existing type metadata pipeline
- Removes the need to remember to run `pnpm run docs:api`, simply running `pnpm run docs:build` (or `pnpm run docs:dev` and viewing the page) will update the types. To manually update all the types.md without the cache you can run `pnpm docs:validate --types`
- Maintains the same speed as current `pnpm run docs:api` script
- Supports Hot Reloading Typedocs
- Build time caching for typedocs and highlighting per entrypoint
- Using [Typescript Language Service API](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/wiki/Using-the-Language-Service-API), reduces single page typedoc generation from `4s` to `0.3s` (**93%** decrease) with subsequent navigations in `0.15s`
- Improved Developer Experience for (Cmd/Ctrl)+Clicking imports in VS Code
- Cleaner diffs for generated files using markdown
- CI checks for Markdown content (e.g. Vale) now run on the typedocs
- Committed files are copied 1:1 into llms.txt markdown version
- Types can be viewed [directly in GitHub](https://github.com/dav-is/base-ui/blob/davis/improved-typegen/docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/accordion/types.md#accordion), which may improve Github Copilot's understanding of the repo
- Adds support for class exports like `Dialog.Handle`
- All hardcoded type tables replaced with automated pipeline (e.g. `useRender` and other hooks)
- Add namespaced types like `AlertDialog.Trigger.State`, or `Checkbox.Root.ChangeEventDetails`
- Known types within the page can link to other types, like `className: string | ((state: AlertDialog.Popup.State) => string | undefined)` will have `AlertDialog.Popup.State` available in a popover: https://deploy-preview-2932--base-ui.netlify.app/react/components/alert-dialog#AlertDialog.Popup-className
- Adds `@example`s to markdown output
- Adds more type information into search index
- Decreased `pnpm docs:dev` server render time up to `~43%` by shifting this compute to build time (allowing caching).
- Negligable increase in uncached `pnpm docs:dev` server response time
- ~25% decrease of `pnpm docs:dev` server response time with a warm cache (page already loaded in previous session)
- ~37% decrease of `pnpm docs:dev` server response time with a hot cache (page already loaded in current session)
- ~32% decrease in `Generating static pages` portion of `pnpm docs:build` (an uncached portion of the build)

What's the new workflow? When I create a new component and a new docs page, what files do I have to create manually and what are autogenerated (and how)?

Having this information in the README and AGENTS.md could be helpful for other humans and agents.

> To manually update all the types.md without the cache you can run pnpm `docs:validate --types`

Why does the "validate" command update anything?

> What's the new workflow? When I create a new component and a new docs page, what files do I have to create manually and what are autogenerated (and how)?

Simply create a `types.ts` file next to the respective `page.mdx` file and import it into the page. `types.md` is an autogenerated file. To create a new component:

1. Create the component's page. e.g. `docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/button/page.mdx`
2. Create the component's types component. e.g.  `docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/button/types.ts`
```ts
import { Button } from '@base-ui/react/button';
import { createTypes } from 'docs/src/utils/createTypes';

export const TypesButton = createTypes(import.meta.url, Button);
```
3. Import the `TypesButton` component to the page.
```mdx
# Button

This is a button.

## API Reference

import { TypesButton } from './types'

<TypesButton />
```
4. Start the dev server `pnpm docs:dev` and load the new component's page: `http://localhost:3005/react/component/button`. The `types.md` is automatically generated. If you don't want to view the component in the browser before committing, just run `pnpm docs:build` and the file will be created.

If the component has multiple parts, use `createMultipleTypes()`:
```ts
import { Checkbox } from '@base-ui/react/checkbox';
import { createMultipleTypes } from 'docs/src/utils/createTypes';

const { types, AdditionalTypes } = createMultipleTypes(import.meta.url, Checkbox);

export const TypesCheckbox = types;
export const TypesCheckboxAdditional = AdditionalTypes;
```
and add multiple sections to the page:
```mdx
# Checkbox

This is a checkbox.

## API reference

import { TypesCheckbox } from './types';

### Root

<TypesCheckbox.Root />

### Indicator

<TypesCheckbox.Indicator />
```

> Having this information in the README and AGENTS.md could be helpful for other humans and agents.

Good idea. I added some details to both [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/dav-is/base-ui/blob/davis/improved-typegen/AGENTS.md#documentation) and [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/dav-is/base-ui/blob/davis/improved-typegen/CONTRIBUTING.md#documentation)

> Why does the "validate" command update anything?

The validate command is primarily intended to run in CI to detect and fail whenever a committed file is out of sync. When something is out of sync, the CI job will give you a specific command to run to quickly update only the out of date file. `pnpm docs:validate "(docs)/react/components/button"` will run very quickly. During normal development, it is best to run `pnpm docs:dev` or `pnpm docs:build`, as they benefit from the cache. Today, the build takes a bit of time, but eventually it will be faster than the validate command. The naming is meant to nudge the user towards running a build.

## Codex Review

### Findings
No blocking issues found in this patch.

#### 1. 🟡 [Non-blocking] Typedoc migration drops the inline type-detail affordances that master added
Impact: Readers lose the inline way to inspect richer type details in API tables. Non-raw type references now fall back to plain links, and property references no longer open any inline detail UI, which is a noticeable regression from the richer API-reference UX already on master.

Evidence: [docs/src/components/TypeRef/TypeRef.tsx#L67-L73](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/6de04ee5bfb732cafe9f050b47a54ce1017a5ab1/docs/src/components/TypeRef/TypeRef.tsx#L67-L73) returns a plain <a> for every non-raw type, making the ReferenceTable branch at [#L90-L94](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/6de04ee5bfb732cafe9f050b47a54ce1017a5ab1/docs/src/components/TypeRef/TypeRef.tsx#L90-L94) unreachable for component/hook/class types. [docs/src/components/TypePropRef/TypePropRef.tsx#L17-L31](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/6de04ee5bfb732cafe9f050b47a54ce1017a5ab1/docs/src/components/TypePropRef/TypePropRef.tsx#L17-L31) now renders property references as bare anchors only. On master, complex prop/type cells still expose inline detail affordances via [docs/src/components/ReferenceTable/ReferenceAccordion.tsx](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/6de04ee5bfb732cafe9f050b47a54ce1017a5ab1/docs/src/components/ReferenceTable/ReferenceAccordion.tsx) and the removed [docs/src/components/ReferenceTable/ReferenceTableTooltip.tsx](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/master/docs/src/components/ReferenceTable/ReferenceTableTooltip.tsx).

Recommendation: Restore the previous inline popover/tooltip behavior, or at minimum remove the non-raw early return so known component/hook/class types still open the new ReferenceTable popover instead of degrading to plain links.

#### 2. 🟡 [Non-blocking] The new callable reference-table paths have already drifted
Impact: Hook and function API docs are implemented twice and already disagree on how to render a simple return type with detailedType. That makes follow-up fixes easy to miss and increases the chance that hook/function docs quietly diverge again.

Evidence: The hook path in [docs/src/components/ReferenceTable/ReferenceTable.tsx#L61-L145](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/6de04ee5bfb732cafe9f050b47a54ce1017a5ab1/docs/src/components/ReferenceTable/ReferenceTable.tsx#L61-L145) and the function path in [#L150-L229](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/6de04ee5bfb732cafe9f050b47a54ce1017a5ab1/docs/src/components/ReferenceTable/ReferenceTable.tsx#L150-L229) are nearly identical. They have already drifted at the simple return-value block: hooks wrap detailedType in CodeBlock.Root at [#L133-L139](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/6de04ee5bfb732cafe9f050b47a54ce1017a5ab1/docs/src/components/ReferenceTable/ReferenceTable.tsx#L133-L139), while functions render detailedType raw at [#L225-L229](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/6de04ee5bfb732cafe9f050b47a54ce1017a5ab1/docs/src/components/ReferenceTable/ReferenceTable.tsx#L225-L229).

Recommendation: Extract the shared hook/function rendering into one helper, or at least centralize the return-value rendering so the two paths cannot diverge on formatting/behavior.

#### 3. ℹ️ [Informational] The new select test reintroduces React.useLayoutEffect despite repo guidance
Impact: This is not a correctness bug, but it reintroduces a pattern the repo explicitly avoids. Leaving new examples behind makes future patches more likely to keep using the wrong hook.

Evidence: [packages/react/src/select/root/SelectRoot.test.tsx#L1008-L1020](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/6de04ee5bfb732cafe9f050b47a54ce1017a5ab1/packages/react/src/select/root/SelectRoot.test.tsx#L1008-L1020) uses React.useLayoutEffect(...) directly. The repo guidance in [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/6de04ee5bfb732cafe9f050b47a54ce1017a5ab1/AGENTS.md) says to use useIsoLayoutEffect instead of React.useLayoutEffect.

Recommendation: Swap that test helper to useIsoLayoutEffect so new code stays aligned with the repo’s required hook convention.

### Confidence: 3/5
Moderate confidence. I reviewed the full branch diff with targeted passes over the handwritten runtime/docs changes, plus independent AGENTS/history/simplification sweeps, but the PR is very large and contains extensive generated-doc churn alongside unrelated commits.

### Notes
The branch carries several commits beyond the docs-infra migration itself, so the findings above focus on issues that are still visible in the full master...head review rather than on generated-file noise.

review_comments.body:
result` is never returned, so the intended "## Types" heading is dropped. Additionally, using `splice(3)` mutates the parsed AST array and returns only the tail; this makes the output dependent on a fixed node count and currently discards the heading you just constructed. Consider returning a concatenated array (e.g., `return [...result, ...parseMarkdown(typesContent).slice(3)]`) so the heading is preserved and the parse output isn’t mutated.
```suggestion
  return [...result, ...parseMarkdown(typesContent).slice(3)];
```

review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,55 @@
+/**
+ * demoProcessor.mjs - Process demo component directories
+ *
+ * This module handles loading and converting demo code examples
+ * into markdown code blocks for documentation.
review_comments.body:
The file header comment appears copy/pasted from the demo processor and does not match this module’s purpose (it processes typedoc/types markdown). Update the header to reflect what this file does so future maintenance is less error-prone.
```suggestion
 * typedocProcessor.mjs - Process Typedoc types markdown
 *
 * This module resolves Typedoc components in MDX files to their generated
 * types markdown, parses that markdown, and returns AST nodes to be
 * inserted into the documentation.
```

This webpack rule matches any file path ending in \`types.ts\`, which is very broad and can unintentionally apply the precomputed-types loader to unrelated \`types.ts\` modules. It would be safer to scope the rule to the intended directory/pattern (e.g., only under \`docs/src/app/**/types.ts\`) to prevent accidental loader application as the codebase grows.

review_comments.body: This is only temporary
I see that the types.md file already has full content. Why do we need to add each section separately here?

This structure also allows overriding the description (see the [merge props docs page](https://github.com/dav-is/base-ui/blob/9ac821e14138ea2ed1c23821e358c0fcedc45655/docs/src/app/(docs)/react/utils/merge-props/page.mdx?plain=1#L71-L85)) and allows introducing the parts in any section of the page. The heading structure of the page.mdx mirrors that of the rendered page for more predictable linking between pages (e.g. if alert dialog adds a link `[Dialog.Root](../dialog/page.mdx#root)`), the links work in markdown when editing and on the website. It also works naturally with the table of contents generator without an additional rehype plugin.

Eventually, I'd like to add a lint script that automatically adds a link to the types.md file for better DX:

```mdx
## API Reference

import { TypesCheckbox } from './types'

### Root

A custom description.

<TypesCheckbox.Root hideDescription />

[See Types](./types.md#root)
```

The See Types link is removed during build so it doesn't appear on the website.

It also mirrors a similar API of Base UI: to get the types for `<Checkbox.Root />`, you just use `<TypesCheckbox.Root />`

Each part is also typed, so you can't use `<TypesCheckbox.Unknown />` without an error

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use a published @mui/internal-docs-infra package version**

Pointing `@mui/internal-docs-infra` at a `pkg.pr.new` URL makes installs depend on a preview host instead of the package registry, which is brittle for CI/proxy environments and can break `pnpm install` for the whole workspace when that host is blocked or unavailable. Pin this dependency to a published npm/canary version so docs build and validation jobs remain reproducible.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prefix re-export links with hash for in-page navigation**

This link uses the raw slug as `href`, but these values are anchor ids in the same reference table, so without a `#` prefix the `Link` component treats it as a route path rather than an in-page anchor. On pages with `multiple` types, clicking “Re-Export of …” can navigate to a non-existent relative URL instead of jumping to the referenced type section.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Did a first pass. I think we need to improve the UX a bit, but it looks promising. **UX** - I find confusing that when clicking `Accordion.Item.ChangeEventDetails`, the type inside the popup is called `AccordionItemChangeEventDetails`. Are both names publicly exported in the package? I assume users will use `Accordion.Item.ChangeEventDetails`? - The way we make types linkable is too magical, and potentially confusing. Once the user clicks "Back" or "Hide", the content is gone and I think it won't be easy for many users to know what's going on or how to go back to see the type, especially if they just landed on the page by following a link. "How do I see the type again?". This is the current UX: - When users click a type in the popover, the popover contents get inlined in the page. When clicking "Back", the content is gone, until the user opens the popover and clicks the type again. Why would a user want to see the popover contents inline? Only to get the link? Then, wouldn't it be enough when clicking the type name inside the popover to update the url so users can copy it? Same as we do when clicking a prop name inside an accordion item in the props table. - When landing on a url that contains the type hash, the type is displayed inline again, this time with the "Hide" button instead of "Back". Again, how a user can see this again? Q: Do we really need linking to types? Is linking to props enough? e.g. linking to the `onOpenChange` prop of the `Accordion.Item` let users see it's using `Accordion.Item.ChangeEventDetails` and they can click it to know more. If we want to allow linking to types, I'd argue that having an accordion with the types at the end of the page would be better than displaying/hiding types temporarily inline on the page. --- **UI** - Adding `text-underline-offset: 2px` to the popover trigger makes the dotter underline look better. before/after - I wonder if we need the close button at all. We could add the arrow to the popover (same as we do in tooltips) and just rely on interaction outside to close the popover. _If we keep the close button 👇_ The close button it's misaligned (see screenshot). 8x8 it's too small IMO. 12x12 would work better (same as chevrons in prop tables), although it'd look chunky so we'd need to change the icon. - I'd try removing the bottom border in the popover header.
